items.title: Gold tops $5,000 as Trump's Iran ultimatum fuels safe-haven rush

featured_image.name: Oil prices hit six-month highs after Trump warns Iran of 'bad things' if there's no deal

items.description: Gold prices pushed above $5,000 an ounce on Friday, propelled by escalating tensions between the United States and Iran and persistent uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's interest rate path. The advance came after President Donald Trump gave Tehran a 10-to-15-day deadline to reach a nuclear deal, warning of "bad things" if diplomacy fails.[1][2]

items.title: US 'totally' rejects global AI governance at New Delhi summit

featured_image.name: US 'totally' rejects global AI governance: White House adviser

items.description:
UN Secretary-General António Guterres used the closing day of the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on Friday to formally announce that 40 members have been confirmed for the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, a body he said would work to "make human control a technical reality — not a slogan."[1][2]

The declaration came on the final day of the five-day summit — the fourth annual global AI gathering, and the first to be hosted in a developing country — where dozens of heads of state, tech executives, and ministers gathered to debate how to govern a technology advancing faster than the institutions trying to regulate it.[3][1]

items.title: New study warns Antarctic Peninsula faces irreversible damage without rapid emissions cuts

featured_image.name: Scientists: We are witnessing irreversible changes in Antarctica

items.description: A new study modeling the best- and worst-case futures for the Antarctic Peninsula warns that the choices made this decade will determine Antarctica's fate for centuries — and that only aggressive emissions reductions can prevent catastrophic and irreversible transformations in one of the planet's most vulnerable regions.

items.title: India signs U.S.-led Pax Silica pact on AI and chips

featured_image.name: US promotes AI sovereignty and exports at India AI impact summit

items.description:
Dozens of world leaders and ministers gathered at the India AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi this week, with a Leaders' Declaration expected to be adopted Friday outlining a shared roadmap for global AI governance and collaboration. The five-day summit — the fourth in a series of global AI convenings and the first hosted by a developing nation — drew heads of state from 20 countries, hundreds of tech executives, and an estimated 250,000 visitors to the Bharat Mandapam convention center.[1][2][3]

The event produced a flurry of diplomatic and commercial activity, headlined by the signing of the Pax Silica Declaration between India and the United States, massive investment pledges from major technology firms, and the unveiling of a new U.S. initiative to deploy AI expertise abroad.

items.title: Ukraine eyes billions in defense exports after first wartime sales approved

featured_image.name: Ukraine to open battlefield-tested arms export centres ...

items.description:
Ukraine expects to export "several billion dollars" in military goods and services in 2026, a senior defense official told Reuters, marking a dramatic reversal from the arms export ban Kyiv imposed after Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.[1][2]

Davyd Aloian, deputy secretary of Kyiv's National Security and Defence Council, said a state commission approved the majority of 40 export applications from defense producers earlier this month — the first wartime export licenses granted since the war began. "Taking into account ready-made products, spare parts, components, and services that can be provided, it amounts to several billion dollars," Aloian told Reuters in an interview published Thursday.[3][2]

The export potential is "significantly higher" than pre-war levels, Aloian said. Before 2022, Ukraine typically ranked among the world's top 15 arms exporters, with average annual sales of roughly $400 million over three decades, according to data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.[2][4][5]

items.title: New nanodevices turn evaporation and pressure into electricity

featured_image.name: Nanodevice produces continuous electricity from evaporation

items.description: Two teams of researchers — one in Switzerland, the other in Australia — have independently developed nanodevices capable of generating electricity from everyday physical processes, offering fresh avenues for sustainable, battery-free power. Both studies, published this week in Nature Communications, demonstrate how nanoscale engineering can turn evaporating saltwater and mechanical pressure into usable energy.

items.title: Gold hovers near $5,000 as Iran tensions and Fed outlook collide

featured_image.name: Gold advances on U.S.–Iran tensions as markets weigh Fed policy path

items.description:
Gold clung to the $5,000-an-ounce level on Friday, caught between safe-haven demand fueled by escalating U.S.-Iran brinkmanship and a strengthening dollar that has put the metal on course for a weekly loss. Spot gold dipped slightly to around $4,983 per ounce in early Asian trading, down roughly 1% for the week, while U.S. gold futures for April held just above $5,000.[1]

The tug-of-war encapsulates a market hypersensitive to two fast-moving storylines: a potential military confrontation in the Middle East and a Federal Reserve that appears in no hurry to cut interest rates.
